hunks.baseline: Warm sunshine, a cool breeze, and even wisps of pure white cloud.
hunks.sol: Warm sunshine, a cool breeze, and wisps of pure white cloud.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps that was why someone who was always living as though pressed for time suddenly spoke to the coachman, who was about to set off in a hurry.
hunks.sol: Perhaps that was why someone who always seemed pressed for time suddenly spoke to his coachman just as the man was about to set off in a hurry.

hunks.baseline: All he had to do was follow orders, after all.
And as a coachman, he much preferred guiding the horses slowly and safely to shouting at people to get out of the way.
hunks.sol: All he had to do was follow orders, after all. And he much preferred guiding the horses slowly and safely to shouting at people to get out of the way.

hunks.baseline: The coachman glanced sideways. A sturdy wall, built high in two or three layers like a fortress, came into view.
hunks.sol: The coachman glanced sideways. A sturdy wall, built up in two and three layers like a fortress, filled his view.

hunks.baseline: On an ordinary day, perhaps not. But at this pace, it would take a full fifteen minutes to reach the end of that wall.
hunks.sol: At their usual pace, it was one thing. At this rate, it would take a full fifteen minutes to reach the end of that wall.

hunks.baseline: The coachman silently marveled. This enormous estate stood not on the outskirts, but right in the center of a city. Prime real estate among prime real estate.
hunks.sol: The enormous estate stood not on the outskirts, but right in the heart of the city. The land was as valuable as it came.

hunks.baseline: The fact that the family owned so much land in the very heart of the city was proof enough of its tremendous power, but that wasn’t what amazed the coachman most.
hunks.sol: Owning so much of it was proof enough of the family’s tremendous power, but that wasn’t what amazed the coachman most.

hunks.baseline: There was probably no more fitting description.
That was the cold reality, and not just the coachman but everyone nearby had thought so.
hunks.sol: There had been no better way to describe it. That was the cold reality, as the coachman and everyone else nearby had seen it.

hunks.baseline: Yet no one could have guessed.
That a family slowly declining, its past glory behind it, would rise in barely more than two short years to become the power ruling over an entire city.
hunks.sol: Yet no one could have guessed that a family slowly declining, its past glory behind it, would rise in barely more than two years to rule an entire city.

hunks.baseline: *Just goes to show, you never know what’ll happen in this world.*
hunks.sol: *Just goes to show, you never know what’ll happen.*

hunks.baseline: Muttering to himself, the coachman looked up at the flag rising high above the stone wall.
The silk fluttered in a breeze from somewhere, and four characters written in a bold, flowing hand caught his eye.
hunks.sol: The coachman looked up at the flag flying high above the stone wall. A breeze caught the silk, and four characters written in a bold, flowing hand caught his eye.

hunks.baseline: The owner of that enormous estate, and a family that had become a symbol of Shanxi Province.
hunks.sol: The owners of that enormous estate had become a symbol of Shanxi Province.

hunks.baseline: The changes surrounding the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been swift and undeniable.

hunks.baseline: The pavilions and walls, once shabby and crumbling, had been repaired until they looked as solid as a fortress. The martial artists, supplied with fine weapons and elixirs, now had a righteous spirit in their eyes the coachman had never seen before.
hunks.sol: The changes to the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been swift and unmistakable. The pavilions and walls, shabby and crumbling when the coachman first saw them, had been repaired until they looked as solid as a fortress. Supplied with fine weapons and elixirs, the family’s martial artists now had a righteous light in their eyes that hadn’t been there before.

hunks.baseline: The entrance, once crowded with debt collectors demanding payment for the reckless Third Young Master’s unpaid bills, was now so packed you could hardly set foot inside—but for entirely different reasons.
hunks.sol: The entrance, once crowded with debt collectors demanding payment for the reckless Third Young Master’s unpaid bills, was now so packed you could hardly set foot there—but for entirely different reasons.

hunks.baseline: There were wealthy merchants from other regions, come to entrust their business to the Jin Family Escort Bureau. There were shopkeepers of every kind, lined up to pay tribute at the end of each month, as well as martial arts sects and Branch Leaders under the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
hunks.sol: Merchants from other regions came to entrust their business to the Jin Family Escort Bureau. At the end of each month, shopkeepers of every kind lined up to pay tribute, along with the martial arts sects and Branch Leaders under the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

hunks.baseline: So many important people from all over Shanxi Province came and went that the threshold was worn down. Some people with nothing better to do even loitered around the Jin Family of Taiyuan, chatting about what they’d seen and heard.
hunks.sol: So many of Shanxi Province’s most important people came and went that they nearly wore out the threshold. Some people with nothing better to do even loitered nearby, spreading whatever they’d seen and heard.

hunks.baseline: Just like the two men squatting beside the wall at the roadside right now.
hunks.sol: Just like the two men squatting beside the roadside wall now.

hunks.baseline: “What do you mean, ‘don’t tell me’? I’ve been devoted to her from the start.”
hunks.sol: “What do you mean, ‘again’? I’ve been devoted to her from the start.”

hunks.baseline: “Cut the nonsense. If your wife catches you, she’ll beat you to death—and then I’ll get killed, too.”
hunks.sol: “Cut the nonsense. If your wife catches you, she’ll beat you to death—and I’ll get killed, too.”

hunks.baseline: “Good grief. You’re a man, and you’re scared? Just answer my question. Didn’t she come today, either?”
hunks.sol: “Good grief. You call yourself a man, getting scared like that? Just answer my question. Didn’t she come today, either?”

hunks.baseline: “Have you considered that one good whack from your wife might make everything go dark? And calling her Shanxi’s foremost beauty hardly does her justice. She leads the Mount Heng Sword Sect despite being a woman—and she’s formidable. If you cross her the wrong way, you won’t walk away in one piece.”
hunks.sol: “Have you considered that one good whack from your wife might make everything go dark? And Shanxi’s foremost beauty is only part of it. She leads the Mount Heng Sword Sect despite being a woman, and she’s formidable. Cross her the wrong way and you won’t walk away in one piece.”

hunks.baseline: The man gazed dreamily into space, then suddenly swallowed.
hunks.sol: The man gazed dreamily into space, then swallowed.

hunks.baseline: The two men’s low conversation gradually faded away.
hunks.sol: The two men’s voices gradually faded.

hunks.baseline: The coachman, who’d been listening to them, gave a quiet laugh and took hold of the reins he’d let slacken for a moment.
hunks.sol: Listening from his seat, the coachman gave a quiet laugh and gathered up the reins he’d let slacken for a moment.

hunks.baseline: The carriage, drawn by four fine horses, crossed the main road slowly, just as his employer had asked.
hunks.sol: Drawn by four fine horses, the carriage made its slow way down the main road, just as his employer had asked.

hunks.baseline: In the past, a single four-horse carriage would have taken up half the street. But now the road was several times wider, and the crowds packed into it simply moved aside a little and carried on with their conversations.
hunks.sol: In the past, a single four-horse carriage would have taken up half the street. But now the road was several times wider, and the crowds packed into it simply moved aside a little and carried on talking.

hunks.baseline: Most of what they said was ordinary gossip, but from the coachman’s perspective, some of it was worth listening to.
hunks.sol: Most of what they said was idle chatter, but some of it was worth the coachman’s attention.

hunks.baseline: “Have you all heard the rumors? The Jin Family of Taiyuan’s blacksmith shop has been making nothing but weapons lately.”
hunks.sol: “Have you heard? The Jin Family of Taiyuan’s blacksmith shop has been making nothing but weapons lately.”

hunks.baseline: “I thought you were about to say something important. That’s been going on for a while, hasn’t it? The Jin Family of Taiyuan is a Murim sect. It’s hardly strange.”
hunks.sol: “I thought you were about to tell me something new. They’ve been doing that for a while, haven’t they? The Jin Family is a Murim family. It’s hardly strange.”

hunks.baseline: “True. But for the past six months, they’ve been dealing exclusively in weapons. If you want to buy farming tools, you’ll have to go at least as far as Gohyeon.”
hunks.sol: “True. But for the past six months, they’ve dealt exclusively in weapons. If you want farming tools, you’ll have to go at least as far as Gohyeon.”

hunks.baseline: “Well, now. Gohyeon’s a good three or four days on foot. Luckily, the tools we bought ahead of time are sturdy enough that we won’t need to buy more.”
hunks.sol: “Well, now. Gohyeon’s a good three or four days on foot. Luckily, the tools we bought earlier are so sturdy we won’t need more.”

hunks.baseline: “That’s because the craftsmen Old Man Jang brought with him are so good.”
hunks.sol: “That’s because the craftsmen Old Man Jang brought with him know their trade.”

hunks.baseline: “Hey, don’t call him Old Man Jang. The Jin Family of Taiyuan trusts him with important work. We ought to call him Master Jang Taebo now.”
hunks.sol: “Hey, don’t call him Old Man Jang. The Jin Family of Taiyuan trusts him with important work. You ought to call him Elder Jang Taebo now.”

hunks.baseline: “Ah, it’s just a habit. Anyway, the more I think about it, the more worried I get. Things in the martial world are supposed to be tense these days. Do you think something big is really about to happen…?”
hunks.sol: “Ah, it’s a habit. Anyway, the more I think about it, the more worried I get. They say things in the martial world are tense these days. Do you think something big is about to happen…?”

hunks.baseline: “Put your worries aside and finish your game of Go. Dark Heaven or whatever can make all the trouble it wants; in the end, it’s a Murim affair. The Great Nation is out there, and the Jin Family of Taiyuan is standing firm right here. What’s there to worry about?”
hunks.sol: “Put your worries aside and finish your game of Go. Dark Heaven or whatever can make all the trouble it wants; in the end, it’s a Murim affair. We have the Great Nation farther afield and the Jin Family of Taiyuan standing firm right here. What’s there to worry about?”

hunks.baseline: “I only said it because the rumors coming from all over don’t sound good. Things up in the northern plateau, which had been quiet for the past year or two, too. The currents in the martial world don’t seem normal.”
hunks.sol: “I only brought it up because the rumors coming from all over don’t sound good. And things up on the northern plateau have changed after being quiet for the past year or two. Something isn’t right in the martial world.”

hunks.baseline: “What’s going on in the northern plateau now? The Jin Family of Taiyuan must have gone out and wiped out the mounted bandits.”
hunks.sol: “What’s going on up north now? I thought the Jin Family of Taiyuan had wiped out the mounted bandits.”

hunks.baseline: “Do mounted bandits disappear just because someone uproots them once? They’re weeds. They keep cropping up. And a few merchant caravans that headed north last month…”
hunks.sol: “Do mounted bandits disappear just because you uproot them once? They’re like weeds. They keep coming back. And a few merchant caravans that headed north last month…”

hunks.baseline: Just as he was silently licking his lips, curious about the rest of the story he hadn’t managed to hear, his employer—who had been staring out at the scenery without a word all the way out of the main road—suddenly spoke.
hunks.sol: He was still trying to catch the rest of the story as the carriage left the main road when his employer, who had spent the ride silently watching the scenery, suddenly spoke.

hunks.baseline: “Everyone has a lot to worry about. Then again, when it’s happening around you, it’s hard not to notice.”
hunks.sol: “Everyone has a lot to worry about. Then again, it’s happening around them. How could they not notice?”

hunks.baseline: “I mean those people. You’ve been listening with your ears pricked up this whole time, so why are you acting so surprised?”
hunks.sol: “I mean those people. You’ve had your ears pricked up this whole time. Why are you so surprised?”

hunks.baseline: “You’ve never spoken to me first like this before, so I was caught off guard.”
hunks.sol: “You’ve never spoken to me first while we were traveling, so it caught me off guard.”

hunks.baseline: “Ah. Well, when you put it that way, I suppose.”
hunks.sol: “Ah. Well, I suppose it would.”

hunks.baseline: The coachman glanced over his shoulder. Through the beaded curtain, he caught a glimpse of his employer nodding as if it were nothing.
hunks.sol: The coachman glanced over his shoulder. Through the pearl-bead curtain, he caught a glimpse of his employer nodding as though it were nothing.

hunks.baseline: The skin powdered pure white, and lips red as cherries, too.
hunks.sol: He also glimpsed skin powdered white and lips red as cherries.

hunks.baseline: *No matter how I look at it…he’s definitely acting differently than usual.*
hunks.sol: *He’s definitely acting differently today.*

hunks.baseline: The coachman had served him for nearly a year, but after all he’d seen and experienced, his employer remained a mystery.
He was always smiling, but for some reason it never seemed like a genuine smile. And there was only one occasion when he ever spoke first to the coachman.
hunks.sol: The coachman had served him for nearly a year, but his employer remained a mystery. He was always smiling, yet somehow it never seemed genuine. And there was only one occasion when he ever spoke to the coachman first.

hunks.baseline: *But today he spoke first, and he hasn’t even looked at his bamboo slips while we’ve been on the road.*
hunks.sol: *But today he spoke first, and he hasn’t even looked at his bamboo slips on the road.*

hunks.baseline: His high-ranking employer was always busy. There was a mountain of work to handle and people to meet everywhere.
hunks.sol: His high-ranking employer was always busy. He had a mountain of work to handle and people to meet everywhere.

hunks.baseline: The coachman had watched him like that for the past year, so it was only natural that his employer’s mood today felt so unfamiliar.
Maybe that was why a pointless curiosity, one he would never normally have let show, instinctively moved his lips.
hunks.sol: After nearly a year of seeing him like that, perhaps it was only natural that today’s change felt so strange. Perhaps that was why the coachman let a pointless curiosity he would normally have kept to himself slip out.

hunks.baseline: The coachman regretted the question as soon as he asked it. There was nothing to gain by upsetting his employer—especially when his employer was a high-ranking official.
hunks.sol: The coachman regretted the question the moment he asked it. Nothing good could come of upsetting his employer, especially one so high-ranking.

hunks.baseline: But his employer proved far more generous than the coachman had expected.
hunks.sol: But his employer was more forgiving than he’d expected.

hunks.baseline: “Hm. Something happened? Yes, it did. I heard some unpleasant news not long ago.”
hunks.sol: “Hm. Something happened? Yes, I suppose it did. I heard some bad news not long ago.”

hunks.baseline: “No, why apologize over something like this? When you bow and scrape too much, it makes me uncomfortable, too. It brings back memories from long ago.”
hunks.sol: “No, why apologize over that? When you bow and scrape too much, it makes me uncomfortable, too. Brings back old memories.”

hunks.baseline: “Memories I never want to return to. For example…”
hunks.sol: “Memories I never want to go back to. For example…”

hunks.baseline: His employer’s voice trailed off, and he suddenly gazed out the window.
hunks.sol: His employer trailed off and gazed out the window.

hunks.baseline: “Something like going out into the street after going three whole days without food, singing to impress people in silk robes.”
hunks.sol: “Going three whole days without food, then standing in the street singing to please people dressed in silk. Memories like that.”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, don’t get the wrong idea. I’m not saying that to make you feel bad. It’s just something that happened.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, don’t get the wrong idea. I’m not saying it to make you feel bad. It’s just something that happened.”

hunks.baseline: The coachman’s mouth fell open at the unbelievable past of such a high-ranking person. His employer, meanwhile, watched the people passing slowly by and smiled faintly.
hunks.sol: The coachman’s mouth fell open at the thought that someone of such high standing had lived through that. His employer watched the people passing slowly by and smiled faintly.

hunks.baseline: “It’s nice to see everyone looking so happy.”
hunks.sol: “It’s good to see them all.”

hunks.baseline: But in someone’s memory, it was also a brand that would never fade.
hunks.sol: But in someone’s memory, it remained a brand that would never fade.

hunks.baseline: The days spent doing everything he could to escape the shackles that had gripped his throat since birth flashed past.
hunks.sol: The days he had spent doing everything he could to escape the shackles that had gripped his throat since birth flashed past.

hunks.baseline: “I managed somehow back then…but can I do it this time, too?”
hunks.sol: “I managed it somehow back then…but can I do it this time, too?”

hunks.baseline: The quiet mutter was carried away by the wind.
hunks.sol: The quiet mutter scattered on the wind.

hunks.baseline: The coachman didn’t dare say another word. He kept guiding the horses onward, while his employer took in everything slowly passing by.
hunks.sol: The coachman didn’t dare say another word. He kept guiding the horses while his employer took in everything passing slowly around him.

hunks.baseline: And as the destination drew nearer, the hoofprints in the ground grew clearer. At last, he knew the time had come.
hunks.sol: As they drew nearer to their destination, hoofprints in the dirt came into clearer view. At last, his employer knew the time had come.

hunks.baseline: His employer suddenly spoke, then nodded at the coachman’s question.
hunks.sol: His employer nodded at the coachman’s question.

hunks.baseline: “Yes, a favor. And an apology, too, for not having been very kind to you until now.”
hunks.sol: “Yes, a favor. Consider it an apology, too, for not being very warm toward you until now.”

hunks.baseline: “Th-there’s no need to say that, sir. If you need anything, please just give me the order. Deputy Military Commissioner.”
hunks.sol: “Th-there’s no need to say that, sir. If you need anything, please give me an order, Deputy Military Commissioner.”

hunks.baseline: “I’m going to get off here. Go to Honghwaru right away and tell them. Or should I say the Lower District Sect’s Shanxi branch?”
hunks.sol: “I’ll get off here. Go to Honghwaru right away and tell them. Or should I say the Lower District Sect’s Shanxi branch?”

hunks.baseline: “You thought I wouldn’t know, didn’t you? But they’ve probably figured it out to some extent already. No matter how secretly the Embroidered Uniform Guard operates, they can’t avoid that many eyes.”
hunks.sol: “You thought I didn’t know? But they’ve probably noticed something by now. No matter how discreetly the Embroidered Uniform Guard moves, it can’t escape that many eyes.”

hunks.baseline: The fact that Hong Jin knew his identity, and the existence of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, said to act only on the Emperor’s orders.
hunks.sol: Hong Jin knew the coachman’s identity. And the Embroidered Uniform Guard—said to move only on the Emperor’s orders—was here.

hunks.baseline: The coachman couldn’t even tell which of those two things he ought to be more surprised by. Then he realized what he needed to ask.
hunks.sol: The coachman couldn’t decide which shocked him more. Then he realized what he needed to ask.

hunks.baseline: “What would you like me to do, Deputy Military Commissioner?”
hunks.sol: “What would you have me do, Deputy Military Commissioner?”

hunks.baseline: “Tell them everything that’s happened. And have them use every bit of the Lower District Sect’s information network to find one person.”
hunks.sol: “Tell them everything that’s happening. Then have them use every bit of the Lower District Sect’s information network to find one person.”

hunks.baseline: “One person, you say?”
hunks.sol: “One person?”

hunks.baseline: “Someone who can protect us in any situation—or rather, His Highness Prince Shangshan. The most trustworthy person in all Murim.”
hunks.sol: “Someone who can protect us in any situation—no, someone who can protect His Highness Prince Shangshan. The martial artist we can trust most.”

hunks.baseline: Hong Jin spoke slowly, but with emphasis.
hunks.sol: Hong Jin spoke slowly, emphasizing every word.

hunks.baseline: The carriage sped away like the wind, and Hong Jin watched it disappear before suddenly turning around.
hunks.sol: The carriage sped away like the wind. Hong Jin watched it until it vanished, then turned.

hunks.baseline: A group arrived in a rush, the sound of their horses’ hooves growing louder.
hunks.sol: A group of riders descended on him amid the thunder of hooves.

hunks.baseline: “We have an imperial decree. You’ll have to come with us, Deputy Military Commissioner.”
hunks.sol: “By imperial decree, you must come with us, Deputy Military Commissioner.”

hunks.baseline: “For now… Well, fine.”
hunks.sol: “For now… All right, then.”

hunks.baseline: Then he set off toward his young lord.
hunks.sol: Then he walked toward his young lord.
